question: How are NYC crashes distributed across the days of the week, 2013 to 2025?

options.denominator: None; cumulative crash counts from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31
options.reason: Raw totals directly show how the full-period crash volume is distributed over the days of the week.
options.answer: Friday had the most crashes (338,800; 15.9% of the 2,132,218 total), while Sunday had the fewest (257,544; 12.1%).
options.interpretation: This framing answers how the full 2013–2025 total is distributed by weekday, with Friday highest and Sunday lowest. It is defensible when cumulative reported-crash volume is the quantity of interest, but it does not show year-to-year changes or average daily frequency.

options.metric: Average number of police-reported crashes per calendar date
options.denominator: Number of dates of that weekday in 2013–2025 (678 or 679 dates)
options.reason: Dividing by weekday-date occurrences adjusts for the small difference in how many dates of each weekday fall in the period.
options.answer: Friday averaged 499.7 crashes per Friday date, the highest rate, while Sunday averaged 379.9 per Sunday date, the lowest.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the typical daily frequency for each weekday and adjusts for weekday-date occurrences, which range from 678 to 679. It likewise shows Friday highest and Sunday lowest, but does not describe year-to-year variation or adjust for traffic volume or other exposure.

answer:
From 2013–2025, Friday had the most reported crashes (338,800; 15.9% of the total), while Sunday had the fewest (257,544; 12.1%). Adjusting for the number of dates of each weekday, Friday averaged 499.7 crashes per date—the highest—while Sunday averaged 379.9, the lowest.
